The brown bottle is near the left target area close to the table centerline on the robot's side, and the green bottle near the corresponding right target area. Merely lifting them slightly at their original positions is insufficient.

## Execution tips

- Select a nearly constant-width body section below the shoulder and above the bottom ridges for continuous pad contact. Avoid sloped shoulders and protruding base ridges to reduce slipping or off-center grasping.
- The gripper opening can be slightly wider than the selected section of the bottle. Before closing, use multiple views if possible to confirm that the fingers are on opposite sides, rather than merely overlapping in the image without enclosing it effectively.
- Both bottles have ample approach space on the robot-facing side. Approach there and orient the grippers in open space to reduce collisions with the drill-like object left of the brown bottle and the stand and orange bottle right of the green bottle.
- Consider using the left arm for the brown bottle and the right for the green bottle. Lift as synchronously as possible while retaining clearance between bottles and grippers to reduce collisions. If one slips, restore tabletop support before adjusting the grasp, avoiding release in the air.
